questions.subject: bio
questions.q: How many daughter cells are produced when one body cell divides by mitosis?
questions.hint: Think of one cell splitting into copies of itself.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement best describes the cells produced by mitosis?
options: They are genetically identical to the parent cell
They have half the number of chromosomes
questions.answer: They are genetically identical to the parent cell
questions.hint: Mitosis is used for growth and repair, so the new cells must match the old ones.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name the type of cell division that produces gametes.
questions.hint: It takes place in the testes and ovaries.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A human body cell contains 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are found in a human sperm cell?
questions.hint: Gametes contain one set of chromosomes, not two.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which of these is NOT a role of mitosis?
questions.hint: Which process needs cells with half the usual number of chromosomes?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What happens to the DNA in a cell before it divides by mitosis?
questions.hint: Each new cell needs a full set of chromosomes.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Meiosis is described as a ___ division because the chromosome number is halved. Write the missing word.
questions.hint: The number of chromosomes goes down.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: How many gametes are produced from one cell that divides by meiosis?
questions.hint: Meiosis involves two divisions in a row.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why does meiosis produce genetic variation?
options: Each gamete receives a different combination of chromosomes
Each gamete is a copy of the parent cell
Gametes have twice as many chromosomes
questions.answer: Each gamete receives a different combination of chromosomes
questions.hint: Think about how chromosomes are shared out between the new cells.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Where are adult stem cells found in humans?
questions.hint: This tissue makes new blood cells throughout life.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In plants, where are stem cells found?
questions.hint: Look for the regions of a plant that keep growing, such as root and shoot tips.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the name of the process by which a stem cell becomes a specialised cell?
questions.hint: The cell becomes different from the original unspecialised cell.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the main advantage of embryonic stem cells compared with adult stem cells?
options: They can differentiate into almost any type of cell
They are always easy to obtain
questions.answer: They can differentiate into almost any type of cell
questions.hint: Adult stem cells can only form a limited range of cells.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A cell divides by mitosis once every 24 hours, and every new cell also divides. Starting with one cell, how many cells will there be after 3 days?
questions.hint: The number of cells doubles each time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why gametes must be produced by meiosis rather than mitosis for sexual reproduction to work.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the chromosome number at fertilisation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Evaluate the use of embryonic stem cells to treat diseases.
questions.hint: Give benefits and concerns (ethical and medical), then reach a judgement.

bss.topic: Climas do Brasil e massas de ar

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual tipo climático predomina na Amazônia?
questions.hint: Pense na região perto da linha do Equador, quente e muito chuvosa.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual característica é típica do clima semiárido do Nordeste?
questions.hint: É o clima do Sertão, com longos períodos de seca.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em qual região do Brasil predomina o clima subtropical?
questions.hint: É a região mais distante da linha do Equador.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual massa de ar quente e úmida se forma sobre a Amazônia?
questions.hint: Ela se forma sobre o continente, numa área de floresta e muita umidade.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quais são as características da massa Polar atlântica (mPa)?
options: Fria e seca, vinda do Pacífico
questions.hint: Ela se forma sobre o oceano, no sul do continente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama a queda brusca de temperatura que às vezes ocorre na Amazônia quando a massa Polar atlântica avança até lá?
questions.hint: O nome vem da sensação de frio repentino.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em um climograma, o que geralmente representam as barras verticais?
options: A umidade do ar em cada hora
questions.hint: A linha costuma representar outra variável.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a característica principal do clima tropical típico do Brasil Central?
options: Chuva bem distribuída o ano todo
questions.hint: Pense nas duas estações bem marcadas do Cerrado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o clima tropical de altitude tem temperaturas mais amenas que o tropical típico?
options: Porque ocorre em áreas mais elevadas
Porque fica mais perto do Equador
Porque recebe a massa Equatorial continental
questions.answer: Porque ocorre em áreas mais elevadas
questions.hint: A temperatura diminui conforme se sobe.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual massa de ar, quente e úmida, se forma sobre o oceano Atlântico e atua no litoral leste do Brasil?
questions.hint: Ela se forma na zona tropical, sobre o mar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a característica da massa Tropical continental (mTc)?
questions.hint: Ela se forma sobre uma área continental no interior da América do Sul, longe do mar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama a chuva provocada pelo encontro de uma massa de ar fria com uma massa de ar quente?
questions.hint: O nome vem da 'frente' que se forma entre as duas massas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que a temperatura média anual de Porto Alegre é menor que a de Manaus?
options: Porque Porto Alegre está em maior latitude
Porque Porto Alegre está mais perto do Equador
Porque Manaus recebe a massa Polar atlântica com mais frequência
questions.answer: Porque Porto Alegre está em maior latitude
questions.hint: Compare a distância de cada cidade até a linha do Equador.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Um climograma mostra temperaturas entre 25 °C e 28 °C o ano inteiro e mais de 2.000 mm de chuva por ano. Que clima ele representa?
questions.hint: Calor constante e muita chuva.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique como a atuação da massa Polar atlântica influencia o inverno nas regiões Sul e Sudeste.
questions.hint: Pense em temperatura, frentes frias e geadas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que as chuvas no Sertão nordestino são escassas e irregulares.
questions.hint: Considere como as massas de ar chegam à região e o papel do relevo.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which formula is used to calculate the gross profit margin?
questions.hint: A margin compares a profit figure with sales.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business has revenue of $200,000 and gross profit of $80,000. Calculate its gross profit margin (%).
questions.hint: Divide gross profit by revenue, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business has revenue of $500,000 and profit of $50,000. Calculate its profit margin (%).
questions.hint: Profit ÷ revenue × 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business makes a profit of $60,000 and has capital employed of $400,000. Calculate its ROCE (%).
questions.hint: Profit ÷ capital employed × 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does return on capital employed (ROCE) measure?
options: How efficiently a business uses its capital to generate profit
How quickly a business can pay its short-term debts
How much stock a business holds
How many customers a business has
questions.answer: How efficiently a business uses its capital to generate profit
questions.hint: Think about the money invested in the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Gross profit = revenue minus ___. Write the missing term.
questions.hint: These are the direct costs of the products sold.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which change is most likely to increase a business's gross profit margin?
options: Finding a cheaper supplier of materials
Paying higher wages to office staff
questions.answer: Finding a cheaper supplier of materials
questions.hint: Gross profit is affected only by revenue and direct costs.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm's gross profit margin stays the same, but its profit margin falls. What is the most likely reason?
options: Its cost of sales has fallen
questions.hint: What is subtracted between gross profit and profit?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A shop has revenue of $80,000 and cost of sales of $50,000. Calculate its gross profit margin (%).
questions.hint: First work out gross profit.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business has a gross profit margin of 25% and revenue of $120,000. Calculate its gross profit in dollars.
questions.hint: 25% of revenue.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which stakeholder group is most likely to use ROCE when deciding whether to invest in a company?
questions.hint: Who wants a return on the money they put in?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why should a business compare its profitability ratios with previous years or with competitors?
options: A single ratio means little on its own
It makes the ratios more accurate
It is required for every sale
questions.answer: A single ratio means little on its own
questions.hint: Is 12% good or bad? It depends on what you compare it with.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Using ratios to assess a business's performance is called ___ analysis. Write the missing word.
questions.hint: The word is in the name of the figures being used.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business has a ROCE of 12% and capital employed of $250,000. Calculate its profit in dollars.
questions.hint: Rearrange the ROCE formula.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain one limitation of using profitability ratios to judge a business's performance.
questions.hint: Think about what the figures do not show, or how old they are.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A company's ROCE fell from 14% last year to 8% this year. Analyse two possible reasons for this fall.
questions.hint: Consider changes in profit and changes in capital employed.

chem.topic: Alcohols: manufacture of ethanol and its uses

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which raw material is used to make ethanol by fermentation?
questions.hint: Fermentation uses a renewable resource.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Name the microorganism used to ferment sugar into ethanol.
questions.hint: It is also used to make bread rise.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which conditions are used for fermentation?
options: Room temperature with plenty of oxygen
questions.hint: Living cells carry out this reaction, and it is anaerobic.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why is fermentation not carried out at a high temperature such as 80 °C?
options: The enzymes in yeast would be denatured
The sugar would turn into ethene
The reaction would need more oxygen
questions.answer: The enzymes in yeast would be denatured
questions.hint: Yeast relies on proteins that are damaged by heat.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What are the products of the fermentation of glucose?
questions.hint: One product is a gas that makes bubbles.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Glucose ferments: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. How many moles of ethanol are produced from 1 mole of glucose?
questions.hint: Read the number in front of ethanol in the equation.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which catalyst is used in the hydration of ethene to make ethanol?
questions.hint: It is an acid catalyst.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which conditions are used for the catalytic addition of steam to ethene?
questions.hint: It needs a high temperature and a high pressure.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The ethene used to make ethanol is obtained by ___ long-chain alkanes from crude oil. Write the missing word.
questions.hint: This process breaks large molecules into smaller ones.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is one advantage of making ethanol by fermentation?
options: It uses a renewable raw material
It is a fast, continuous process
questions.answer: It uses a renewable raw material
questions.hint: Where does the sugar come from?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is one advantage of making ethanol by hydration of ethene?
options: It is fast and produces pure ethanol
It uses a renewable raw material
questions.answer: It is fast and produces pure ethanol
questions.hint: Compare the speed and purity of the two methods.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which separation method is used to obtain concentrated ethanol from the fermentation mixture?
questions.hint: It separates liquids with different boiling points.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of ethanol, C₂H₅OH. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.hint: Count every atom: 2 C, 6 H and 1 O.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Balance the equation for the complete combustion of ethanol: C₂H₅OH + __O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. What number goes in the gap?
questions.hint: Count the oxygen atoms on the right, then subtract the one already in ethanol.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Ethanol made by fermentation can be called a biofuel. Why?
options: It is made from plant material
It does not produce carbon dioxide when burned
questions.answer: It is made from plant material
questions.hint: 'Bio' refers to living things.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Compare the manufacture of ethanol by fermentation and by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene.
questions.hint: Consider raw materials, conditions, rate, purity and whether the process is batch or continuous.

comp.topic: Databases: single-table databases, fields, records and primary keys

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In a single-table database, what is a record?
options: A complete set of data about one item, shown as a row
A single category of data, shown as a column
questions.answer: A complete set of data about one item, shown as a row
questions.hint: Think of one line of data about one thing.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In a single-table database, what is a field?
options: One category of data, shown as a column
A complete row of data about one item
questions.answer: One category of data, shown as a column
questions.hint: Think of a heading such as 'Surname'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: State the name given to the field that uniquely identifies each record in a table.
questions.hint: It is the 'key' that tells records apart.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data type is most suitable for storing a person's date of birth?
questions.hint: The value is a day, month and year.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A field called HasPaidFee can only be Yes or No. Which data type is most suitable?
questions.hint: Only two possible values.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data type should be used for a telephone number such as 01632 960123?
questions.hint: Think about the leading zero and the space.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which field would make the best primary key in a table of library books?
questions.hint: Which value could never be shared by two books?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A table holds data about 250 cars, with 8 fields for each car. How many records are in the table?
questions.hint: One record per car.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A table holds data about 250 cars, with 8 fields for each car. How many individual data items does the table store?
questions.hint: Records × fields.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data type is most suitable for a Price field storing values such as 12.99?
questions.hint: The value has a decimal part.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which data type is most suitable for a NumberOfPages field?
questions.hint: Pages are counted in whole numbers.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A field stores a single grade letter such as A, B or C. Which data type is most suitable?
questions.hint: It is one letter only.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement about a primary key is true?
options: It must contain a unique value for every record
It must always be a text field
It can be left blank for some records
Every table needs at least two
questions.answer: It must contain a unique value for every record
questions.hint: Think about what 'identifies' means.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why Surname would not be a suitable primary key in a table of students.
questions.hint: Could two students share the same value?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A vet stores data about pets in one table. Suggest a suitable primary key and explain your choice.
questions.hint: Think of a value created to be different for every pet.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Identify two fields, each with a suitable data type, for a table storing details of films shown at a cinema.
questions.hint: Think of text, number and date values about a film.

econ.topic: Applied microeconomics: demand and supply diagrams in current events

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A frost destroys much of the coffee harvest. Which change happens in the coffee market?
questions.hint: Less coffee can be produced at every price.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: After the frost, what happens to the equilibrium price and quantity of coffee?
questions.hint: Follow the new curve to the new equilibrium.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A popular online star promotes a brand of trainers. What happens in the market for those trainers?
questions.hint: Tastes and preferences have changed.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The government introduces an indirect tax on sugary drinks. What happens to the supply curve?
questions.hint: The tax raises producers' costs.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Incomes fall during a recession. What happens to demand for a normal good?
questions.hint: Normal goods are bought more when incomes rise.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The price of petrol rises sharply. What is the likely effect on demand for large petrol cars?
questions.hint: Petrol and cars are used together.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What term describes the price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied?
questions.hint: The market is 'balanced' here.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: New technology cuts the cost of making solar panels. What happens to equilibrium?
questions.hint: Lower costs shift supply to the right.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: If a price is set above the equilibrium price, what results?
questions.hint: Compare quantity supplied with quantity demanded.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A heatwave raises demand for ice cream while higher milk prices raise costs. What can be said for certain?
questions.hint: Both shifts push one variable the same way.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: On a demand and supply diagram, what is shown on the vertical axis?
questions.hint: The horizontal axis shows quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: The government gives a subsidy to wheat farmers. What happens to the supply of wheat?
questions.hint: A subsidy lowers producers' costs.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Concert tickets are resold for far more than their original price. What does this suggest?
options: Excess demand at the original price
Excess supply at the original price
questions.answer: Excess demand at the original price
questions.hint: More people wanted tickets than were available.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using a demand and supply diagram, explain the effect of a new tax on cigarettes on the market for cigarettes.
questions.hint: Which curve shifts? Describe the new price and quantity.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A news report says avocado prices have risen as avocados became more popular. Explain why the price has risen, using demand and supply.
questions.hint: Think about a change in tastes.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A drought reduces the wheat harvest. Explain how this could affect the market for bread.
questions.hint: Wheat is a raw material for bread.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a 45-minute narrative composition, roughly how long should you spend planning?
questions.hint: Enough to plan, but leave most time for writing.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is a common simple plan for a short story?
questions.hint: Think of the shape of a story.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which opening is most likely to engage the reader?
options: The door had been locked for eleven years, until tonight.
This is a story about a door.
Once upon a time there was a door.
I am going to tell you about a door.
questions.answer: The door had been locked for eleven years, until tonight.
questions.hint: Which one makes you ask a question?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does 'show, don't tell' mean?
options: Reveal feelings through actions, dialogue and detail
questions.answer: Reveal feelings through actions, dialogue and detail
questions.hint: Let the reader work out the feeling.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the term for a narrative told by a character using 'I'?
questions.hint: Count the pronoun: I, you, or he/she.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the best way to manage a 350–450 word story?
options: Focus on one key event over a short time
Add as many plot twists as possible
questions.answer: Focus on one key event over a short time
questions.hint: The word limit is tight.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which technique is used in 'Footsteps. Closer. Then nothing.'?
questions.hint: Look at the length of each sentence.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What term describes a scene that moves back to an earlier time in the story?
questions.hint: It looks back in time.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which ending is generally most effective in a timed story?
options: One that links back to the opening
'And then I woke up – it was all a dream.'
Stopping mid-sentence when time runs out
Introducing a new character in the last line
questions.answer: One that links back to the opening
questions.hint: A circular structure feels complete.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why should you leave about 5 minutes at the end?
options: To check spelling, punctuation and paragraphing
questions.answer: To check spelling, punctuation and paragraphing
questions.hint: Accuracy is also marked.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What punctuation marks go around the words a character speaks?
questions.hint: They open and close the dialogue.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence best appeals to the senses?
options: The smell of burnt toast drifted under the door.
questions.answer: The smell of burnt toast drifted under the door.
questions.hint: Which one could you smell, hear or see?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When should you start a new paragraph in a narrative?
options: When the time, place, speaker or topic changes
questions.answer: When the time, place, speaker or topic changes
questions.hint: Remember TiPToP.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write an opening sentence for a story called 'The Last Train' that creates mystery.
questions.hint: Hold back some information.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain two ways a writer can build tension near the climax of a story.
questions.hint: Think about sentence length, pace and detail.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In note form, give a setting, a main character and the central problem for a story called 'The Storm'.
questions.hint: Keep each note short and specific.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In a 45-minute unseen poetry answer, what should you do first?
options: Read the poem and the question carefully, at least twice
Count the syllables in every line
questions.answer: Read the poem and the question carefully, at least twice
questions.hint: Understanding comes before analysis.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What term describes the voice speaking in a poem?
questions.hint: It is not always the poet.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What is enjambment?
options: When a sentence runs over a line break without punctuation
A pause in the middle of a line
questions.answer: When a sentence runs over a line break without punctuation
questions.hint: Look at the ends of lines.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: 'The city is a sleeping beast' is an example of which device?
questions.hint: There is no 'like' or 'as'.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A poem uses words such as 'grey', 'hollow' and 'cold'. Which word best describes its tone?
questions.hint: What mood do these words share?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What is a pause in the middle of a line of poetry called?
questions.hint: It is often marked by a full stop or comma mid-line.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What does a strong analytical paragraph usually include?
options: A point, a short quotation and analysis of its effect
questions.answer: A point, a short quotation and analysis of its effect
questions.hint: Think PEA or PEE.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: 'Whispering waves wandered' is an example of which device?
questions.hint: Listen to the first sounds.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: A poem with no regular rhyme or metre is written in…
questions.hint: It is 'free' of fixed patterns.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: What term describes a group of lines in a poem?
questions.hint: It is like a paragraph in poetry.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Why should you comment on a poem's structure?
options: Because form and structure help create meaning
To show you can count lines
questions.answer: Because form and structure help create meaning
questions.hint: How does the shape support the ideas?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Which phrase is the most precise way to begin analysis?
options: The image evokes a sense of loss
questions.answer: The image evokes a sense of loss
questions.hint: Choose a verb that explains an effect.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In the line 'The clock, the clock, the clock kept on', what does the repetition mainly do?
options: Emphasises the slow, relentless passing of time
questions.answer: Emphasises the slow, relentless passing of time
questions.hint: Think about the rhythm of a ticking clock.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Why is it useful to explore more than one interpretation in an unseen poetry answer?
questions.hint: Think about what examiners reward.

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Read: 'My grandmother's hands were maps / of every field she'd ever worked.' Explore the effect of the metaphor.
questions.hint: What might the lines on a map suggest?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Explain how you would plan and structure a 45-minute response to an unseen poem.
questions.hint: Think about timing, paragraphs and an overview.

fmath.topic: Integrating eˣ, 1/(ax + b) and trigonometric functions

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ e^(3x) dx.
questions.hint: Divide by the coefficient of x.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ (2x + 1)⁴ dx.
questions.hint: Raise the power by one, then divide by the new power and by 2.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ 1/(4x + 3) dx.
questions.hint: The integral of 1/u is ln|u|; remember the 4.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ cos(2x) dx.
questions.hint: Integrating cos gives sin; divide by 2.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ sin(3x) dx.
questions.hint: Integrating sin gives minus cos.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ e^(2x + 1) dx.
questions.hint: Differentiate each option to check.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ 6/(2x − 1) dx.
questions.hint: Take out the 6 and divide by 2.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of e^(2x) dx, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use [(1/2)e^(2x)] between the limits.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to π/2 of cos x dx.
questions.hint: Integrate to sin x, then substitute.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to π/6 of sin(2x) dx, giving an exact fraction.
questions.hint: Use [−(1/2)cos 2x] and cos(π/3).

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find the exact value of ∫ from 1 to 3 of 1/x dx.
questions.hint: Use ln 1 = 0.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find the exact value of ∫ from 1 to 4 of 1/(2x + 1) dx.
questions.hint: Use a law of logarithms: ln 9 − ln 3.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ (3x − 2)⁻² dx.
questions.hint: Add one to the power and divide by the new power and by 3.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Evaluate ∫ from 0 to 1 of (2x + 1)³ dx.
questions.hint: The antiderivative is (2x + 1)⁴/8.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Find ∫ (4e^(2x) − cos x) dx.
questions.hint: Integrate each term separately.

questions.subject: fmath
questions.q: Explain why ∫ 1/(2x) dx can be written both as (1/2)ln|x| + c and as (1/2)ln|2x| + c.
questions.hint: Use ln|2x| = ln 2 + ln|x|.

fre.topic: Grammar consolidation: plus-que-parfait and passé composé in narratives

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct word (plus-que-parfait): « Quand je suis arrivé, le film ___ déjà commencé. »
questions.hint: Commencer takes avoir; the subject is 'le film'.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct word (plus-que-parfait): « Elle ___ partie avant midi. »
questions.hint: Partir takes être.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French using the plus-que-parfait: 'I had finished.'
questions.hint: Imperfect of avoir + past participle.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French using the plus-que-parfait: 'We had eaten.'
questions.hint: Use the 'nous' form of avoir in the imperfect.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct agreement: « Mes sœurs étaient ___ (sortir). »
questions.hint: Feminine plural subject with être.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write the plus-que-parfait of 'tu / voir'.
questions.hint: Voir takes avoir; its participle is irregular.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: In « J'ai perdu le livre que j'avais acheté », which tense is « j'avais acheté »?
questions.hint: It happened before losing the book.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the best ending: « Quand nous sommes arrivés à la gare, le train… »
questions.hint: The train left before we arrived.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Translate into French using the plus-que-parfait: 'They (masculine) had left.'
questions.hint: Partir takes être, so the participle agrees.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Complete in the plus-que-parfait: « Il s'___ réveillé tard. »
questions.hint: Reflexive verbs take être.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write the plus-que-parfait of 'vous / prendre'.
questions.hint: Prendre takes avoir; its participle is irregular.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: Elle avait déjà fait ses devoirs quand son ami a téléphoné.
Elle a déjà fait ses devoirs quand son ami avait téléphoné.
Elle avait déjà faire ses devoirs quand son ami a téléphoné.
Elle était déjà fait ses devoirs quand son ami a téléphoné.
questions.answer: Elle avait déjà fait ses devoirs quand son ami a téléphoné.
questions.hint: Which action happened first?

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Choose the correct translation of 'I had already seen that film.'
questions.hint: 'Had seen' needs the plus-que-parfait with avoir.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Write two sentences in French about a past holiday: use one verb in the passé composé and one in the plus-que-parfait.
questions.hint: Show which action happened first.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Explain in English when the plus-que-parfait is used, and give one French example.
questions.hint: Think of 'had done' in English.

questions.subject: fre
questions.q: Which auxiliary does 'aller' use in the plus-que-parfait?
questions.hint: Aller is a verb of movement, like venir and partir.

geog.topic: Tourism as a growing industry (detailed specific example)

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which is a reason for the global growth of tourism?
questions.hint: What makes travel easier for more people?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What term describes tourism that aims to protect the environment and benefit local people?
questions.hint: It starts with 'eco'.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is 'leakage' in tourism?
options: When tourist money flows out of the host country
questions.answer: When tourist money flows out of the host country
questions.hint: Think about foreign-owned hotels and imported food.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What is a honeypot site?
options: A place that attracts large numbers of tourists
questions.answer: A place that attracts large numbers of tourists
questions.hint: Visitors 'swarm' to it.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What does the multiplier effect mean in tourism?
options: Tourist spending creates further jobs and income locally
The number of tourists doubles every year
questions.answer: Tourist spending creates further jobs and income locally
questions.hint: Follow the money as it is spent again.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which is an environmental cost of mass tourism?
options: More litter and pressure on water supplies
questions.answer: More litter and pressure on water supplies
questions.hint: Choose the negative effect on nature.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which is a social benefit of tourism?
options: Improved local services such as roads and clinics
questions.answer: Improved local services such as roads and clinics
questions.hint: Choose the positive effect on people.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What word describes jobs available only at certain times of the year?
questions.hint: Think of summer or winter only.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which strategy makes tourism more sustainable?
options: Limiting visitor numbers at fragile sites
Building large hotels on the beach
questions.answer: Limiting visitor numbers at fragile sites
questions.hint: Which option protects the place for the future?

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: A resort earns $50 million from tourism, and $20 million leaks out of the local economy. What percentage leaks out?
questions.hint: Divide the leaked amount by the total, then × 100.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Why do many tourism jobs in low-income countries pay low wages?
options: Many are low-skilled, such as cleaning or portering
questions.answer: Many are low-skilled, such as cleaning or portering
questions.hint: Think about the type of work.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Which is a typical feature of ecotourism accommodation?
options: Small lodges using local materials and renewable energy
questions.answer: Small lodges using local materials and renewable energy
questions.hint: Low impact, local benefit.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: What term means the maximum number of visitors a place can support without damage?
questions.hint: How much the place can 'carry'.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain two economic benefits of tourism for a developing country.
questions.hint: Think about jobs, income and foreign currency.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Using an example you have studied, evaluate the benefits and costs of tourism.
questions.hint: Weigh the positives against the negatives and reach a judgement.

questions.subject: geog
questions.q: Explain why ecotourism may be more sustainable than mass tourism.
questions.hint: Compare impacts on the environment and local people.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which city did the 1980 shipyard strikes that led to Solidarity begin?
questions.hint: It is a port on the Baltic coast.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: In which year was Solidarity founded?
questions.hint: It followed the summer strikes.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What was Lech Wałęsa's job at the shipyard?
questions.hint: He worked with wiring.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What was Solidarity?
options: An independent trade union not controlled by the Communist Party
A branch of the Polish army
questions.answer: An independent trade union not controlled by the Communist Party
questions.hint: It represented workers.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which economic issue helped spark the 1980 strikes?
questions.hint: Think about the cost of everyday shopping.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Roughly how many members did Solidarity have by 1981?
questions.hint: It was a mass movement in a country of about 36 million.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: When was martial law declared in Poland?
questions.hint: About 16 months after Solidarity began.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why did the Polish government declare martial law?
options: To crush Solidarity and avoid a possible Soviet invasion
questions.answer: To crush Solidarity and avoid a possible Soviet invasion
questions.hint: Think about what happened in Hungary and Czechoslovakia.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What happened to Solidarity under martial law?
options: It was banned and many leaders were arrested or interned
It took control of the army
questions.answer: It was banned and many leaders were arrested or interned
questions.hint: The government wanted to stop it.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: How did the Catholic Church help the opposition in Poland?
options: It gave moral support and places to meet
questions.answer: It gave moral support and places to meet
questions.hint: Most Poles were Catholic.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What agreement, signed in August 1980, allowed free trade unions in Poland?
questions.hint: It is named after the city where it was signed.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which prize did Lech Wałęsa receive in 1983?
questions.hint: It recognises work for peace and rights.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which 1989 talks between the government and Solidarity led to partly free elections?
questions.hint: Both sides sat as equals.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Why was Solidarity a challenge to Soviet control?
options: It was a mass movement independent of the Communist Party
It was run by Soviet officials
questions.answer: It was a mass movement independent of the Communist Party
questions.hint: Communist states allowed only one party.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Explain why Solidarity gained so much support in Poland in 1980–81.
questions.hint: Think about the economy, leadership and the Church.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: How significant was martial law for the Solidarity movement? Explain your answer.
questions.hint: Consider the short term and the long term.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is plotted on the vertical axis of a histogram with unequal class widths?
questions.hint: It is not just 'frequency'.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which formula gives frequency density?
questions.hint: Density is 'per unit' of width.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The class 10 < x ≤ 20 has a frequency of 30. Find its frequency density.
questions.hint: Class width is 10.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The class 20 < h ≤ 25 has a frequency of 15. Find its frequency density.
questions.hint: Find the class width first.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A class has width 40 and frequency density 0.5. Find its frequency.
questions.hint: Frequency = density × width.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: In a histogram, the bar for 0 < t ≤ 5 has frequency density 4. Find the frequency.
questions.hint: Multiply by the class width.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The class 30 < m ≤ 50 has a frequency of 18. Find its frequency density.
questions.hint: Class width is 20.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The class 5 < x ≤ 15 has frequency density 2.4. Find its frequency.
questions.hint: Width × density.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: In a histogram, what does the area of each bar represent?
questions.hint: Area = width × height.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A histogram has two bars: 0 < x ≤ 10 with frequency density 1.2 and 10 < x ≤ 30 with frequency density 2.5. Find the total frequency.
questions.hint: Find each bar's frequency, then add.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The class 60 < w ≤ 80 has frequency density 1.5. Estimate how many values lie between 60 and 70.
questions.hint: Use only half of the bar's width.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The class 20 < x ≤ 40 has frequency density 3. Estimate how many values in this class are greater than 25.
questions.hint: The part above 25 has width 15.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Heights: 0 < h ≤ 10 (frequency 8), 10 < h ≤ 15 (frequency 12), 15 < h ≤ 30 (frequency 9). What is the greatest frequency density?
questions.hint: Work out the density of each class.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: On a histogram, the class 0 < t ≤ 4 has frequency 12 and its bar is 6 cm tall. The class 4 < t ≤ 10 has frequency 9. How tall, in cm, is its bar?
questions.hint: Find each frequency density and use the same scale.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Why do we use frequency density when class widths are unequal?
options: So that bar area is proportional to frequency
So all bars are the same height
questions.answer: So that bar area is proportional to frequency
questions.hint: Wide classes would otherwise look too big.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain why plotting frequency instead of frequency density could make a histogram with unequal class widths misleading.
questions.hint: Think about how the eye judges the size of a bar.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which energy transfer takes place in a d.c. motor?
questions.hint: The motor makes something move.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What type of current does a d.c. motor use?
questions.hint: The letters d.c. stand for it.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Name the part that reverses the current in the coil every half turn.
questions.hint: It is a ring cut into two halves.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Why must the current in the coil reverse every half turn?
options: So the coil keeps turning in the same direction
questions.answer: So the coil keeps turning in the same direction
questions.hint: Without it, the coil would rock back and forth.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the job of the brushes?
options: To keep electrical contact with the rotating commutator
questions.answer: To keep electrical contact with the rotating commutator
questions.hint: The coil spins but the wires do not.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which change would increase the turning effect on the coil?
questions.hint: More current means a bigger force.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which rule predicts the direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field?
questions.hint: It is the rule for motors.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, what does the thumb represent?
questions.hint: First finger = field, second finger = current.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What happens if the direction of the current is reversed?
options: The motor turns the opposite way
questions.answer: The motor turns the opposite way
questions.hint: The force on each side reverses.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What happens if both the current and the magnetic field are reversed?
options: The motor turns the same way as before
questions.answer: The motor turns the same way as before
questions.hint: Two reversals cancel out.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Apart from increasing the current, which change increases the turning effect?
options: Increasing the number of turns on the coil
questions.answer: Increasing the number of turns on the coil
questions.hint: More wire in the field means more force.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Why is the coil often wound on a soft iron core?
options: To concentrate the magnetic field and increase the turning effect
questions.answer: To concentrate the magnetic field and increase the turning effect
questions.hint: Iron is easily magnetised.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: At which position is the turning effect on a flat coil greatest?
options: When the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field
When the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field
Only when the brushes touch the gap
questions.answer: When the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field
questions.hint: When are the forces furthest from the axle?

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: At the vertical position the brushes briefly touch the gap in the commutator. Why does the coil keep turning?
options: The current flows in both halves
questions.hint: It is already moving.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain how a d.c. motor produces continuous rotation.
questions.hint: Mention forces on the coil sides and the commutator.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A student's model motor spins too slowly. Suggest and explain two changes that would make it spin faster.
questions.hint: Think about current, turns and magnets.
